# NOTES: BOOK 1 of 2 — *In the Mayor's Parlour* (J.S. Fletcher, 1922; Hathelsborough; Gutenberg 25424)

## Setting/Places
- Hathelsborough: old borough, market-place (cobbles). High Cross (east, before Moot Hall) and Low Cross (west, facing church). 15th-c.
- St Hathelswide church (13th c., W end, "Virgin and Martyr"). Moot Hall (E end, mediaeval, iron gates, one entrance; flanked by old Mayor's residence/Dr Wellesley's house and bank).
- Curfew from St Hathelswide tower, 60 min after sunset.
- Meadow Gate (N), River Gate (S, to river). Barley Market, Abbey Gate, Farthing Lane (behind Abbey House garden), St Lawrence Lane (behind Moot Hall, narrow, cobbled), Piper's Passage, Copper Alley, Strand Lane, Woolmarket, Little Bailey Gate, Waterdale, Locker St etc.
- Castle: Norman keep, grounds (public garden, Castle Ward). Bull's Snug (secret tavern via passage near High Cross). Chancellor Hotel. Monitor office (up alley off market). Tannery House (Crood). Abbey House (Mrs Saumarez). Acacia Lodge (Brent's house, Castle Ward, bought from John Chillingham for 2,000 guineas). Police station: basement, office on St Laurence Lane, dock with iron corkscrew stair down to cells.
- Clothford: nearby manufacturing city (typewriter firm Green & Polford Ltd; Royal County Hotel; Lingmore Cross Roads).

## Characters
- **John Wallingford**: Mayor, murdered; 41; only son of Rev. Septimus Wallingford (ex-Vicar of Market Meadow, Berkshire); Reading Grammar School; solicitor; came to Hathelsborough ~12 yrs ago as managing clerk; bought practice; Mayor elected by ONE vote; 481st Mayor; Castle Ward councillor; reformer; unmarried; threatened; wrote will a week before death (all to cousin Brent, ~£15,000). Carried red-leather memorandum book.
- **Richard Brent**: cousin, London journalist (Fleet Street), tall, square jaw, grey eyes, brusque, "I guess", "By God"; later buys Acacia Lodge, stands for Castle Ward, loses; loves Queenie.
- **Bunning**: ex-sergeant-major caretaker of Moot Hall, salutes; wife (Mrs Bunning); rooms at back (St Lawrence Lane door). Served Aldershot, Gibraltar, Malta, Cairo, Peshawar.
- **Spizey** (Stephen Spizey): Bellman, Town Crier, Mace-bearer, Apparitor; 40 yrs in office; three-cornered laced hat; gold-lace cloak; mops brow; "I ain't a man—I'm a office!"; caretaker of St Lawrence church, cottage at churchyard corner. Wife **Sarah Jane Spizey**: 6 ft, moon face, charwoman, washed Moot Hall court floor 6–8pm, saw no one.
- **Superintendent Hawthwaite**: borough police, big, bearded, fixed ideas; "slow and sure"; had Scotland Yard man visit; Mrs Saumarez's ex-housemaid his informant.
- **Dr Wellesley**: police-surgeon/physician, tall, clean-shaven, fresh-coloured, handsome, Riverside Ward councillor, Reform man; former suitor of Mrs Saumarez; had side door (Piper's Passage) to Moot Hall; refuses to name his drawing-room caller.
- **Dr Barber**: second doctor. **Dr Carstairs** (Rutherford): red-haired blue-eyed young Scot, assistant, ~3 months.
- **Peppermore**: editor-reporter of *Monitor*, big spectacles, pencil behind ear, ~10 yrs in town; proprietor a Progressive tradesman. Boy assistant **Jimmy Pryder** (red-haired, ~15, son of Sergeant Pryder).
- **Alderman Simon Crood**: Deputy-Mayor, tanner (Tannery House), big, flabby, parchment face, churchwarden pipe, dead-black broadcloth, fob with seals; Town Trustee; later elected Mayor by 2 votes; arrested; "Go you home at once, miss!"
- **Krevin Crood**: Simon's brother, ex-solicitor, ex-Town Clerk, ex-Magistrates' Clerk; pension £156/yr (really £300); tall, spare, ~50, cultured accent, "sub judice"; cicerone, medicine-carrier for Dr Wellesley; arrested.
- **Queenie (Miss Queenie) Crood**: niece of Simon, daughter of Ben Crood (d.; parents died 6 yrs before); dark hair, olive complexion, lustrous eyes; wants stage/London; typed alphabet on Simon's typewriter to prove letter; marries Brent.
- **Mallett** (Stephen Mallett): bank manager, Borough Auditor, Town Trustee; side-whiskers; wife **Mrs Mallett**: handsome, determined, eye-glass, sister of Mrs Coppinger; visited Wellesley and Wallingford (3 visits); fled husband; back in town.
- **Coppinger** (James): Borough Treasurer, Town Trustee, younger; fled with Mallett.
- **Town Trustees**: Crood, Mallett, Coppinger; self-perpetuating three-man financial body.
- **Mrs Saumarez** (Anita): widow of Captain Roderick Francis Saumarez RN (claimed); Abbey House; young, violet eyes, fair hair; wealthy; burned Wallingford's letters in cedar cabinet; secret liaison with Mallett (Royal County Hotel, Clothford). Companion **Mrs Elstrick**: tall, thin, reserved; met Krevin in Farthing Lane; left court before Krevin's statement finished.
- **Epplewhite** (Samuel John): elderly tradesman, Forward Party leader, friend of Wallingford; kept threatening typewritten letter.
- **Tansley**: Brent's solicitor (office next door to Wallingford's); cynical; "Semper eadem".
- **Seagrave**: Coroner of the Honour of Hathelsborough; old, keen, precise; spectacles.
- **Meeking**: barrister for police (prosecutes Krevin/Simon).
- **Cotman**: solicitor for Wellesley. **Stedman**: solicitor for Simon. **Walkershaw**: Borough Surveyor.
- **Mrs Appleyard**: Wallingford's landlady (later Queenie's lodging; "Mother Appleyard").
- **Mrs Marriner**: laundress, Marriner's Laundry.
- **Winifred Wilson**: Wellesley's housemaid, 20, sweetheart Joe Green; told Mrs Lane (Girls' Friendly Society).
- **Louisa Speck**: Mallett's parlour-maid, 26.
- **Nettleton** (Matthew James): Borough Accountant (7 yrs), resigned.
- **Dr Septimus Pellery**: antiquary, ex-resident, Fellow of Society of Antiquaries, Oxford DCL; discovered secret passage 20 yrs before.
- **Owthwaite** (Samuel): Green & Polford mechanic, Hathelsborough native.
- **Welton**: Detective-Sergeant.
- **Robertshaw**: policeman. **Mrs Lane**. **Mr Gates** (horsy). **Simpson** (vet). **Spelliker** (tradesman).
- **Krevin's cell/Little Bailey Gate** lodgings.

## Chronology of Crime & Investigation
- April evening, Wallingford leaves office 5pm; home ~7; leaves books at Abbey House; to Moot Hall; Bunning sees him enter ~7:25.
- Brent arrives ~8:00; finds Wallingford dead across desk; rapier wound through back (heart). Curfew rings.
- Handkerchief fragment (fine cambric) found half-burnt on hearth by Bunning; Hawthwaite locks in safe.
- Coroner's inquest #1 (adjourned 10 days; then inquest #2 after 10 days; then adjourned 1 month).
- Rapier (old Spanish, from curiosity shop, sold few days before) found behind heavy bookcase in Parlour.
- Will found: executed a week before death; witnessed by two clerks.
- Brent refuses Corporation funeral (Town Clerk's visit); says "his murderer's one of 'em."
- Wallingford's threatening letter (typewritten, illiterate phrasing, read at inquest; "bullet through my head or a knife between my ribs" remark to Epplewhite).
- Brent buys Acacia Lodge; poster; Crood elected Mayor by 2 votes.
- Monitor special edition: facsimile letter "WHO TYPED THIS LETTER?" (5,000 copies).
- Brent loses Castle Ward election (~100+ votes); Local Government Board inspector comes; inspector finds nothing.
- Simon & Krevin arrested by Hawthwaite at 6:30pm and ~7pm (on day before committal); Mallett & Coppinger absconded.
- Mrs Mallett's ring/affair revealed (diamond ring receipt from London jeweller).

## Key Testimony
- Brent: Wallingford's Augean stables; "rottenest and most corrupt little town".
- Constable (raw youth): away 6:50 for ~5 min (charge office), 7:45 cellar for paraffin.
- Mrs Spizey: no one came up.
- Epplewhite: Town Trustees; letter from Wallingford; "Don't you ever be surprised..."
- Mrs Saumarez: Wallingford proposed, she refused; Wellesley proposed 2–3 times; "I think there was jealousy."
- Carstairs: Wellesley absent surgery 7:30–7:49 (nineteen minutes); saw him in white linen jacket; Meeting appointment Meadow Gate 7:50 ("ten minutes to eight").
- Bunning: 7:25 up. Dr Barber: death ~45 min before 8:15.
- Walkershaw: connecting wall/door Wellesley house–Moot Hall; oiled; passage ~1 minute.
- Mrs Marriner: handkerchief Wellesley's (French cambric; bought Paris ~1 yr before; dozen). Cotman: maybe wrong basket.
- Winifred: saw Wellesley at 7:45 leave drawing-room door on landing.
- Wellesley: caller was side door, 7:30, refuses name.
- Mrs Mallett: "I was the caller!" 7:30 arrangement (met Wellesley in market 4pm); went to Mayor's Parlour door ~7:35; heard two loud voices quarrelling; left "a little before 7:45"; husband at Conservative Club or Crood's.
- Mrs Bunning: out fetching supper beer 7:30–nearly 8 (Chancellor Vaults); back door left ajar.
- Krevin (at inquest): describes St Lawrence churchyard/lane as hiding place.
- Hawthwaite: Wellesley visited Mrs Saumarez late at night; ex-housemaid informant; Mrs Elstrick & Krevin met 10pm Farthing Lane.
- Owthwaite: Simon brought Semmingford typewriter no. 32,587 to Green & Polford; ordered repair; no hurry.
- Nettleton: Krevin's pension really £300; Town Trustees' secret accounts; Wallingford had red-leather notebook; Corporation "bankrupt".
- Louisa Speck: Mallett's dinner (Mon, Mrs Mallett away at sister Mrs Coppinger's); guests Simon, Krevin, Coppinger; Krevin took clean shirt, collar, handkerchief from drawer; a fine cambric handkerchief with unusually broad hem lay on pile; gone next morning. Simon & Krevin left ~10:45; Coppinger ~11:30.
- Pellery: secret passage through connecting wall/arch across St Lawrence Lane from middle chamber of St Lawrence tower (panelled, 7 compartments per wall; 4th compartment on outer wall slides) into Moot Hall corridor wall (8 ft thick) to Mayor's Parlour (5th panel on left-hand side per Krevin); Hawthwaite & Pellery visited previous day.
- Spizey: Krevin got keys ~7pm ("eyes weren't as strong"); Mrs Spizey: Krevin returned keys just after eight, papers under arm.
- Welton: found in Krevin's writing-case (Little Bailey Gate) 56 papers in Wallingford's hand, several blood-stained; at Simon's desk (Tannery) 17 papers + red-leather memorandum book in Simon's bedroom drawer.

## Krevin's Confession (Ch XXIV)
- Mallett, Coppinger, Simon proposed bribe via Krevin (lawyer-ambassador) to Wallingford: drop investigations; minor reforms credited to him; solicitor practice; Parliamentary support. Krevin's fee: £1,000.
- Krevin went to St Lawrence church ~7; locked himself in; climbed to chamber; through passage ~7:30; looked through panel: parlour empty; then Wallingford + a woman entered (argument; she had watched Mrs Bunning out, slipped in Bunning's back door; she demanded letters; he refused, said they were hold over her; mentioned Wellesley and Mallett).
- Krevin heard thud; door closed; he went in; Wallingford lying across desk; blood on Krevin's fingers. He wiped hand on handkerchief from Mallett's drawer and burned it; took papers and memorandum book; left by passage.
- Woman: **Mrs Saumarez**.

## Ending (Ch XXIV–XXV)
- Brent runs down River Gate, Farthing Lane; climbs 8-ft garden wall of Abbey House; cook says mistress out early on bicycle.
- Waste-basket torn papers; telegram (from Clothford, 7pm previous evening): "Lingmore Cross Roads six-thirty" (from Mallett). Brent pockets it.
- Hawthwaite arrives; Mrs Elstrick gone. Brent: "She's off!"
- Ends: Brent finds Queenie in Mrs Appleyard's garden shelling peas. "THE END."

## Other Notes
- Brent's quotes: "I'm not going to see a woman hang!" (sentiment).
- Peppermore's Mrs Saumarez visit: wants name suppressed; "third man."
- Hathelsborough saying: "as thick as thieves."
- Bull's Snug: Krevin "Sir Oracle."
- Coroner Seagrave: "a mere, formal, crystallizing" etc.
- Spizey sayings: "Precedent!"; "Mischief!"
- Book 1 list of new fiction ads at end (irrelevant).

# NOTES: BOOK 2 of 2 — *Jimmy Quixote* (Tom Gallon; Gutenberg 41754)

Dedication: to Malcolm Watson. Published Hurst & Blackett, 1906.

## BOOK I

**Ch I "Old Paul's Babies"**
- Old Paul = Paul Nannock, tall, light brown hair (thinning), blue eyes, high forehead; Daisley Cross village; house Daisley Place; old servant **Patience** (Patience Roe).
- Old Paul returns from London with parcels (lost list; Jimmy's boots; "full-flavoured" tobacco error); Anthony Ditchburn (lodger; tobacco-craver; "great work" monumental treatise; quotes Horace).
- Children: **Moira** (dark-eyed, dark hair, ~8–9; daughter of Paul's lost love; her mother married richer man, died; Paul took Moira); **Jimmy** (James Larrance, boy; parents lost at sea; guardian embezzled, found shot in Liverpool); **Alice** (Vickery, blonde, prim, curls; mother flung telegram, left her).
- Paul's backstory: as shy young man, first and only love (dark-eyed woman); she left for richer man; later sent for him at death; he took daughter Moira.
- Shawl of many colours bought for Patience.
- Old Paul's "Old Paul" nickname from Moira's explanation.

**Ch II "And Old Paul's Friends"**
- Ditchburn came in storm; stays; Paul pays everything; "Anthony Ditchburn" — learned, tobacco-fond, scornful of children ("rank sentiment"); teaching failed; Rev. **Temple Purdue** (small mild spectacled rector, widower, wife's headstone) teaches children; son **Charlie Purdue** (tall fair, mischievous) joins them.
- **Baffalls**: Daniel Baffall (retired London business, grey eyes, short grey beard, "Mother" wife) and **Flora / Mrs Baffall** (childless; wants children; doll). Baffall: "one of these fine days Mrs. B. will be off with one of 'em."
- Honora Jackman introduced (Baffalls' friend; high voice; single eyeglass; "fine old time"; mercenary; "a rich young man—collecting babies").

**Ch III "Jimmy Quixote"**
- Honora tricks Jimmy (aged ~13) into revealing secret glade in woods; she tries to surprise Paul; Paul sends her away ("biggest baby of the lot"); Jimmy weeps; Paul: "Come on, Jimmy Quixote"—nickname.
- Honora second attempt; Moira thwarts.

**Ch IV "The Eloping Persons"**
- Moira & Paul elope in old chaise, donkey "the Ancient One" (bought from gipsy; chaise 17 shillings); breakfast at inn; "elopement" to Honora who sees them return; Moira's triumph; Moira: "promise never elope with anybody but me."
- Anthony complains Honora "dangerous."

**Ch V "Jimmy's Affections"**
- Honora's farewell (sings Irish song; kisses Moira; wine toast; "Jimmy—I drink to you").
- Honora's letter to Jimmy "yours ever lovingly" (signed Honora Jackman); Jimmy burns it.
- Charlie kisses Moira in race; Jimmy fights Charlie in wood; "Say you're sorry"; Moira pretends.

**Ch VI "Mrs Baffall's Dream"**
- Paul learns he is dying (unnamed illness; "death"); visits Mrs Baffall at night ("Good-night!" not "good-bye"). Paul's message: babies' future.
- Paul dies at foot of stairs (heart? night before will); will unfinished: "To Moira, beloved of my heart now and always, I give——".

**Ch VII "Over the Hills and Far Away"**
- Patience finds body; Moira reads note, tears; burial; Honora returns; takes children off for day.
- **Matthew Shandler** (cadaverous, second cousin on father's side) claims estate; sells house; Patience & Moira to London; Alice to Baffalls; Jimmy to London warehouse (Baffall's contact).
- Jimmy & Moira farewell at hilltop in rain ("I'm going to do big things in London").
- END BOOK I.

## BOOK II

**Ch I "The Call of the World"**
- Moira & Patience live in tiny top rooms, Locker Street, Chelsea; Moira 14; Patience savings.
- Moira goes to opera (Faust) with a girl; kisses her hand.
- Moira writes to Alice; Alice replies (letter: "ALICE VICKERY"; Jimmy's warehouse address). Moira visits Alice's house (footman; Mrs Baffall; Alice: "Poor washed-out thing"). Moira goes to warehouse (Cheapside turning); Jimmy gone (clerks mock).

**Ch II "Jimmy—and a Matter of Food"**
- Jimmy in boarding-house Camden Town (landlady; shoe fight with weedy youth).
- Writing: first story to editor (flaxen-haired; "William" the pale boy); cut to 2,000 words; 16 shillings; paper folds; Jimmy hungry; Holborn court room; British Museum; tea-shop.

**Ch III "The Complete Letter-Writer"**
- Patience writes black-edged letter to Baffalls (boasting: investments, carriage, "Moira ... too gay").
- Baffall suspects bluff; Rev. Purdue; Baffall suggests Charlie live with Moira.
- Anthony begs Rev. Purdue (letter signed "ANTHONY DITCHBURN"; P.S. ten shillings); Purdue sends sovereign and Charlie's address.

**Ch IV "The Man in Print"**
- Charlie visits Locker St (fair, moustache); takes Moira to restaurant (waiter; Bohemia music hall).
- Charlie moves downstairs; Anthony arrives; "Is there anyone here who remembers Jimmy—Jimmy Larrance?"; Anthony found Jimmy in British Museum reading room; Jimmy's story in print ("By James Larrance").
- Moira writes Jimmy; reply "MY DEAR, DEAR MOIRA ... JIMMY."

**Ch V "Another Taste of Bohemia"**
- Anthony fails to find Jimmy (tries Fleet St office; borrows half-crown).
- Moira finds Jimmy's rooms (small court off Holborn; landlady dragon: "robbin' honest people").
- Moira cooks breakfast (rasher, eggs, kettle tea) for Jimmy; Charlie & Anthony arrive; Charlie suggests lunch; Jimmy gets pink cheque, 5 guineas. "Does it always come in like that, Jimmy?" "Mostly like that."

**Ch VI "Charlie Plunges"**
- Charlie's background: flighty mother; father Rev. Purdue.
- Father confronts Charlie (drunk; hospital absent); ultimatum, allowance.
- Charlie borrows, cheats father (books money). Father summons Charlie to Daisley Cross (rectory; churchyard meeting).
- Father gives £50 draft ("last you will ever have from me").
- Charlie tries painting, writing; Jimmy critiques; fails.
- Charlie tells Moira he loves her; kisses; Moira agrees to marry ("I think").

**Ch VII "Dreams"**
- Jimmy's novel; publisher (big-bearded; £6 5s 9d debt later); Bennett Godsby (actor, theatre; play synopsis; £20 + £20).
- Moira comes to Jimmy's rooms to say Charlie asked her to marry; Jimmy: "I cannot see myself ever marrying"; "I hope you'll be very happy."

**Ch VIII "The Sides of the 'Buses O!"**
- Godsby rewrites play; joint authorship; cheques £10 + £10; Mrs Bennett Godsby; newspaper mistakes; printed billing (Godsby first, Larrance small).
- Mrs Baffall, Alice come to theatre; Alice radiant; "We have taken a box."
- Jimmy sees name on 'bus sides.

**Ch IX "The Dawn"**
- Opening night; Jimmy paces; Godsby: "you'll be somewhere about."
- Moira goes to theatre; can't get in; touches Jimmy's name on board: "Jimmy, you might have remembered, dear."
- Moira sleeps in Charlie's room; Charlie, drinking, returns; sleeps with her; "I didn't know, Charlie."
- Dawn; she flees up stairs. END BOOK II.

## BOOK III

**Ch I "It'll Be All Right"**
- Moira pregnant; avoids Charlie. Patience learns; "Dear God!" Charlie: "It'll be all right."
- Charlie borrows from Patience (refused, keys).
- Charlie goes to father (Daisley Cross): "there's a woman"; father: "Get out of my house."
- Charlie crosses road, struck by vehicle in London; dying. Asks for Jimmy.

**Ch II "Jimmy Quixote"**
- Jimmy's success (Godsby, next play commission £100 pink cheque; Alice's suitor Ashby Feak).
- Charlie dies: tells Jimmy of Moira, child, "wronged her"; Jimmy swears to marry Moira. Charlie: "Tell her from me—I said it'd be—be all right!"
- Jimmy writes to Patience; Patience: Moira "wanted you" (said "Jimmy").
- Rev. Purdue: "this was my fault"; Jimmy: "She will be provided for."
- Jimmy tells Moira he'll marry her; "Mrs Larrance"; "we shall go on as before."

**Ch III "Two Ways of Love"**
- Wedding (rain; draughty church; clergyman puzzled; part at church door).
- Money returned by Moira; Moira moves to country; Jimmy's letters ignored.
- Patience tells Jimmy of birth of baby girl named Moira (dark eyes); gives Jimmy address.
- Alice: Ashby Feak returned from exploration (bears, snake bite); Jimmy & Alice meet at National Gallery ("Harbour of Refuge", Fred Walker); Jimmy proposes; Alice agrees; secret.
- Moira visits Jimmy's rooms (late night); holds out hands; talks of baby; says she waited; Ashby Feak bursts in; Moira: "I am Mr Larrance's wife."
- Jimmy: "Yes—there is someone else." (Alice.)

**Ch IV "The Long Night"**
- Anthony Ditchburn (bear-like) walks to Moira's cottage; lodges secretly; steals box of letters ("addressed to James Larrance, Esq."; baby garments); takes letters.
- Anthony takes money from Moira ("sinecure chance"); goes to Jimmy's rooms; Jimmy drunk and degraded.
- Jimmy recounts: Alice married Feak; Jimmy's downfall; Moira's visit (tried to kill her in memory: "Yes—kill me").
- Anthony gets £5; gives Jimmy letters, Jimmy flings them in corner.
- Jimmy's dream: Moira comes at night and writes with him; he works. "The long night was ended... she knew that she had won."

**Ch V "'If I Might Die!'"**
- Jimmy tells Moira he's working; proposes living together; Moira refuses ("I will live with my child alone").
- Jimmy finds letters (pages; "I LOVE YOU"; "The child is yours!"; "If I might die, Jimmy dear——").
- Anthony confesses to Moira; Moira bursts, drives him out ("Go—never let me see you again!").
- Jimmy goes to cottage; Moira gone; Patience: "She will come back to the child."

**Ch VI "The Spirit of Old Paul"**
- Jimmy takes baby (note: "She belongs to me... I want to show her how her mother was once a child"); to Daisley Cross inn.
- Jimmy revisits Daisley Place, woods; talks to baby; Moira listens at door.
- Moira goes to Old Paul's grave; Jimmy finds her; "Jimmy! ... You like the baby?" "She's mine—my baby; you said so," kisses her.
- Patience weeps. Final: "Love had shown them the way... into the brighter promise of a new day." THE END.
